lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Ran 18 moderated usability sessions a quarter from a recruiting panel of 400 customers, so every major release was tested with real account holders before launch.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Raised the onboarding flow's System Usability Scale score from 68 to 104 across two rounds of moderated testing with 20 customers.
- Validated the redesigned app navigation's findability with an open card sort of 30 customers before it shipped.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Apr 2020 - Feb 2022
- Ran the monthly patient survey and rebuilt its reporting dashboard, cutting the time from survey close to published findings from 3 weeks to 4 days.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Wrote the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Championed an inclusive, human-centered design approach to transit wayfinding that delivered meaningful, user-first outcomes.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Check that the portfolio link works and leads directly to relevant case studies.
Remove the date of birth and nationality unless an application requests them.
items.because: They take space and generally aren’t needed on a US résumé.

items.says: Consider dropping the location and dates if you need space.
items.because: Your experience is now more relevant.

items.says: Clarify whether you decided on the three-step design or evaluated it.
items.because: Your ownership of the result should not be overstated.

items.says: Check that the test sample and analysis support the claimed reduction.
items.because: That would make the outcome credible.

items.says: Qualify “every major release” unless you can substantiate it.
Clarify whether 18 sessions was a consistent quarterly rate.
items.because: The current phrasing sounds like a standing guarantee.

items.says: Fix the opening grammar; “Synthesizing” doesn’t fit the rest of the bullet.
Separate what the synthesis produced from what the team changed afterward.
items.because: The 23% drop otherwise reads as an unsupported direct result of affinity mapping.

items.says: Correct or remove the SUS score of 104.
items.because: System Usability Scale scores cannot exceed 100.

items.says: An open card sort does not by itself validate findability in a proposed navigation.
items.because: It helps investigate how people group and label information.

items.says: Make the connection between prototype findings and the shipped design’s effect explicit.
items.because: That distinguishes your research contribution from the completion-rate change.

items.says: Specify what changed in the reporting process, not just the dashboard, if both contributed.
items.because: That would explain the substantial time saving.

items.says: Identify the recommendation or finding that led to two-way texting.
Check whether the before-and-after comparison supports saying texting “cut” missed appointments.
items.because: The change should not be attributed to the feature without support.

items.says: Clarify whether the setup-time reduction applied across studies or to a particular study type.
items.because: “All patient studies” is a broad claim.

items.says: Clarify the period and basis for the 30% support-call comparison.
items.because: That would protect the result.

items.says: Say whether other changes launched at the same time.
items.because: That would protect the attribution of the support-call result.

items.says: Add a project or case-study link if available.
Clarify whether the map was a prototype or a deployed product.
items.because: Readers need to know how to interpret the results.

items.says: Replace the vague “Championed an inclusive…” bullet with a specific responsibility or finding.
items.because: Its adjectives don’t say what you did or what changed.

items.says: The drop from 90 to 60 seconds is a 33% reduction in time, not 50%.
Specify whether route-finding time was measured in testing and with whom.
State the task-success change as 20 percentage points, not an unqualified 20%.
items.because: It went from 65% to 85%.

items.says: Explain how task success was counted across the 12 participants.
items.because: The percentages may represent multiple tasks rather than participants.

items.says: Link the clinic work if you can.
Clarify your role within the three-person team.
Check whether phone bookings fell because more people booked online rather than because demand changed.
Add the comparison basis for the drop in phone bookings if you have it.
Clarify what “six issues” means.
items.because: That specificity would make the testing claim easier to trust.

items.says: Explain how you established that each issue prevented completion.
items.because: That specificity would make the testing claim easier to trust.

items.says: Clarify whether later teams used the handbook specifically to add Spanish-language booking or simply used it while maintaining the pages.
Consider adding other research or analysis tools if you use them and they matter for your target roles.
Correct “interveiws” to “interviews.”
Make sure the A/B testing entry reflects your actual role.
items.because: Methods should be backed up with work examples.

items.says: Account for relevant work since employment ended in June 2025, if any, or be ready to explain the interval.
items.because: The ongoing transit project does not by itself establish employment.
